question: According to Parliament’s Committee on Budgetary Control (CONT), the number of cases of fraud and irregularities in public procurement procedures involving EU funds increased in 2022. More specifically, a CONT Committee report would seem to indicate the most important critical issues to concern the RRF (Recovery and Resilience Facility), where a lack of effectiveness was found in the disbursement process and potentially also as regards the assessment of whether to suspend payments. In view of this: 1.
Is the Commission aware of these weak spots in the area of public funds?
What steps does the Commission intend to take to reduce the irregularities in the disbursement and management of EU funds?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (16.4.2024) The Commission, the European Court of Auditors, the European Anti-Fraud Office (OLAF) and the European Public Prosecutor’s Office (EPPO) carry out activities to ensure that EU budget is spent according to the rules and protected. If a misuse of EU funds is detected, the EU institutions and bodies act within their competences.

All applicable EU rules, such as the Financial Regulation1, the Recovery and Resilience Facility Regulation (RRF)2, the rules applicable to funding managed jointly with the Member States in cohesion and other areas3 and to agricultural funding4, include tailored provisions for the EU budget to be effectively protected from irregularities, fraud, corruption, conflict of interest and unlawful conducts.

Furthermore, OLAF and the Commission publish periodic thematic reports: (i) OLAF’s annual report5 provide details of its investigative work; (ii) the Commission’s ‘PIF’ annual report deal with the protection of the EU’s financial interests6. The EPPO publishes an annual report on its activities too.

With regard to the RRF Regulation, its Article 22 provides that Member States are responsible to ensure the protection of the financial interests of the EU and that the use of funds in relation to measures supported by the RRF complies with the applicable EU and national law, in particular regarding the prevention, detection and correction of fraud, corruption and conflicts of interests.

It also provides for the right of the Commission to reduce proportionately the support under the RRF and recover any amount due to the EU budget or to ask for early repayment of the loan, in cases of fraud, corruption, and conflicts of interests affecting the financial interests of the EU.

Moreover, in order to check that Member States fulfil their obligations, the Commission carries out system audits on national control systems to verify whether the measures in place protect the financial interests of the EU and identify the measures needed to counter weaknesses. To date, the Commission has audited the control systems of all Member States, covering 154 auditees.
Some of them will also be subject to additional audits when and where weaknesses are detected.
